answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with time-locked staking: every identity must lock a deposit that vests over time, so a new identity cannot transact at full weight until its stake has aged through many epochs. At dawn of each cycle only a small fraction releases, so a flood of fresh identities gains almost nothing. An attacker must fund and wait for each fake identity, and the cost ripples outward: the more identities they create, the more capital sits idle and exposed to slashing. One lotus cannot bloom into a swarm, because weight is earned by time and stake, not registration.
